Place **Candidate models** after **Pipeline tuning**. This experimental card
supports continuous regression. It chooses one completed configuration overall,
and one within each candidate method. It does not fit models or construct an
ensemble. All completed evidence is considered, including configurations outside
the former score-based shortlist.

### Chart and tabs

**Overall** compares configurations across methods. Each method tab compares
configurations within that method. Tabs change the view only: the Overall winner
is always the pipeline exported downstream. Method winners are recorded in tuning
review metadata as zero-based trial identities; their complete evaluated pipelines
remain available in the evidence for later ensemble work. Preprocessing may differ
between those pipelines.

Rotate the 3D chart by dragging, zoom with the wheel and inspect points by hovering.
The axes show the primary tuning score, observed prediction rows per second and
P95 absolute error. Method colours remain consistent across tabs. The scene uses
Pythagoras’s standard pale-blue background.

### What the Pareto frontier means

A configuration is **dominated** when another configuration in the current tab
is at least as good on all three criteria and strictly better on at least one:

- Lower RMSE or MAE, or higher R², for Score.
- Higher prediction throughput.
- Lower P95 absolute error.

The **Pareto frontier** is the set of configurations that are not dominated.
Moving from one frontier configuration to another generally means trading one
criterion against another. Frontier membership does not imply that a model has
the best score, or that its performance difference is statistically established.
**Overall** computes the frontier across all candidate methods; each method tab
computes it within that method. A point can therefore be on its method’s frontier
while dominated in Overall. Changing the weights changes the weighted winner,
not the frontier itself.

| Marker appearance | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Method colour | Model method, as identified in the fullscreen legend and hover text |
| Larger, fully opaque circle (size 6) | Pareto frontier configuration |
| Smaller, partially transparent circle (size 4, 65% opacity) | Dominated configuration |
| Large black diamond with white outline | Winner under the current weights |

Size and opacity encode Pareto status; they do not encode model complexity,
uncertainty or viewing distance. Outlines help distinguish points against the
blue background. Duplicate criteria values can overlap. No interpolated frontier
surface is implied. The camera is retained across updates.

Only finite three-coordinate points can be drawn. A score-only winner with missing
prediction diagnostics can still be selected and inspected in the table, but cannot
appear on the 3D chart. Classification and ordinal outcomes are outside this card.

### Weights and automatic selection

The footer slider partitions 100% between **Score**, **Throughput** and **P95
error**. For boundaries a and b, weights are a%, (b−a)% and (100−b)%. Both handles
at the right select 100% Score, the default. Labels update while dragging; selection
is published when a handle is released. The same weights apply in every tab.
There are no Accept, Revert or Selected row actions. Row and point selection only
inspect a configuration; new completed trials can change the weighted winners.

The weighted product is calculated in log space: positive RMSE/MAE and P95 error
are minimized, throughput is maximized. R² is converted to the loss **1−R²**;
weights therefore express proportional changes in that loss, not raw R². The
**Minimum error for weighted products** setting explicitly floors zero and small
losses. Its default is 1e−12. It is in target units for RMSE/MAE and P95, and
dimensionless for the R² loss. Unit changes may require adjusting the floor.
Above the floor, multiplying a criterion by a positive unit conversion does not
change the ranking. Arbitrary shifts and nonlinear transformations can change it.

A missing or invalid positively weighted criterion makes a configuration
ineligible. A zero-weight criterion does not exclude it. Exact weighted-product
ties prefer the three-axis Pareto frontier, then the primary score and finally
the stable trial identity. If no eligible winner exists, the incoming pipeline
passes through without a new selection. Historical read-only evidence is displayed
but never applied as a pipeline.

### Comparison details

All candidate methods are implicitly eligible. Interpretability descriptions
are provided for review and do not certify transparency. Old saved method
filters are ignored and omitted from newly saved configuration.

The flip side shows all eligible configurations in the current tab, the Overall
and method winners, scores, diagnostic evidence and parameter differences. Rows
labelled **Best score (reference)** are emphasised. Selecting a row opens the
comparison details; clearing the selection closes them. **Download** exports the
current tab's eligible table and winner indicators.

**RMSE/MAE** is diagnostic only: the ratio of mean fold RMSE to mean fold MAE.
It describes disproportionate error magnitudes and is unchanged if every error
is multiplied by a constant. It does not quantify absolute tail risk. Perfect
predictions have an undefined ratio, shown as missing. P95 is the mean of
repeat-level 95th absolute-error percentiles, not a pooled percentile. It can miss
very rare extreme errors. Throughput is observed warm validation-batch timing,
including preprocessing, rather than a production benchmark.

Practical equivalence compares configurations against their method's best
primary-scoring trial. It requires suitable repeated shuffled CV and an
application-based tolerance. It does not constrain weighted selection. All tuning
comparisons are exploratory and subject to selection bias. Use independent
validation before making deployment decisions. No automatic ensemble is created.

Weights, floor and comparison settings are saved with the card. Winner
identities are recalculated from current compatible evidence when restoring.
Stale upstream evidence cannot be applied to a changed source.
